roadmap.goal: Story #6247: Lighthouse decides once, on the server, which Work Items in progress are stale and why, and every surface reads that answer. Slice 01 (backend, releasable alone: `lh ... --json` already passes the fields through) writes the pure StalenessPolicy (Doing only; Blocked takes precedence; time in state stale when days > threshold and not Blocked; blocked duration stale when Blocked days >= blocked threshold; 0 turns a trigger off; a TimeInStateWhileBlocked context reason that does not make the item stale; days counted on the instance calendar as of the read's day), carries `isStale` / `staleReasons` on GET teams/{id}/metrics/wip and GET portfolios/{id}/metrics/wip through WorkItemDto.CarryStaleness, and moves the sync-time WorkItemBecameStale signal onto the same policy. Slice 02 (frontend) makes the Time-in-State badge and its tooltip, the Work Items dialog column, the aging chart's dots, the Flow Overview Stale count/RAG and the aging-pace data read the server's fields, drops the staleness threshold props from the badge, the dialog column and the chart (BaseMetricsView keeps its two for hasStaleConfig and the Blocked RAG), and deletes Lighthouse.Frontend/src/utils/staleness/. Done when every DISTILL pending scenario for slices 01 and 02 is un-ignored / un-skipped and green: no `[Ignore(Pending)]` remains in Models/Staleness/StalenessPolicyTest.cs or API/Integration/Staleness/, and no `.skip` remains in TimeInStateBadge.test.tsx, WorkItemsDialog.test.tsx, WorkItemAgingChart.test.tsx, BaseMetricsView.test.tsx (story-6247 describe) or utils/oneStalenessRule.enforcement.test.ts; the three active guards (Blocked items read says nothing, WIP read without a day, StalenessPolicyPurityArchUnitTest) stay green throughout. Slice 03 (lighthouse-clients), docs prose, release notes, evolution record, Stryker and ADO transitions are NOT steps here.
roadmap.paradigm_note: The Hypothesis + state-delta unit mandate from nw-roadmap does not apply, deliberately. Backend is C# + NUnit 4.6 + Moq + WebApplicationFactory, frontend TypeScript + Vitest + RTL; neither test project references a property-testing library (DISTILL: 'FsCheck is not referenced by the test project'; the closed input space is covered by [TestCase] / it.each boundary tables). DISTILL authored every acceptance and policy unit test. The crafter authors no new acceptance test: RED is removing `[Ignore(Pending)]` / `.skip` and watching the test fail as distill/red-classification.md records (all MISSING_FUNCTIONALITY, 0 BROKEN); GREEN is production code. Two classes of test edit are allowed and are named per step: (a) existing tests that the step makes wrong (threshold-driven badge, dialog, chart and Flow Overview tests; the deriveStaleness suite), rewritten onto `isStale` / `staleReasons` or deleted in the same commit as the change that makes them wrong; (b) mechanical arity edits (WorkItemServiceTestBuilder gains the clock). Where a pending test is GREEN_ON_TODAY or will already pass once an earlier step has wired the read, the step names it and says how its RED is demonstrated instead (sabotage by substitution, never by commenting a call out: docs/ci-learnings.md). Steps that touch more than one test file list them all in test_files; test_file names the primary one.
exit_gates: End of every phase: backend suite green with `dotnet test --filter "TestCategory!=Integration&TestCategory!=JiraIntegration&TestCategory!=LinearIntegration&TestCategory!=AdoIntegration&TestCategory!=ServiceNowIntegration"` (exactly 2 Licensing failures in a git worktree are the gitignored valid_not_expired_license.json fixture, not a regression; 10 ReleaseServiceTest failures under load are contention). `dotnet build` zero compiler warnings; the 2 NU1903 advisories on Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR.Common 10.0.12 predate this story and are out of scope.

End of phase 02: `pnpm test` and `pnpm build` green with zero errors and zero warnings in Lighthouse.Frontend/. Run `pnpm exec biome check ./src` read-only FIRST: `pnpm build`'s prebuild is `biome check --write` and rewrites files (and remove any `*/docs` symlinks before it runs).

Before any push: `cd Lighthouse.Backend && dotnet format analyzers Lighthouse.sln --severity info --verify-no-changes --no-restore`, filtered to the union of `git diff --name-only <base>` and `git status --porcelain` (new files are invisible to git diff), with zero findings in a touched or new file. Frontend: Biome clean on every touched file. SonarCloud: no new issue of any severity.

Program.cs is NOT edited by this story, and must not be: WorkItemService is registered by type (`AddScoped<IWorkItemService, WorkItemService>`) and ILighthouseClock is already a registered singleton, so the new constructor parameter in 01-04 resolves without a registration change. CI therefore does not run the full live-connector Integration suite for this change. If a step finds itself editing Program.cs, stop and say why at the hold.

End of phase 01 (slice-01 dogfood and its learning hypothesis): start the backend locally via `Lighthouse.Backend/Start-DevServer.ps1` (or `/run-dev`; NEVER the shared dev instance on :5169, and override the Kestrel keys if a spare port is needed, since ASPNETCORE_URLS is ignored), load demo data, and read `GET /api/latest/teams/{id}/metrics/wip?asOfDate=<today>` for a demo Team, plus the same Team for a past day and one demo Portfolio's `/api/latest/portfolios/{id}/metrics/wip?asOfDate=<today>`. Record: whether any demo Work Item reads `isStale: true` and with which reason (demo Teams and Portfolios set a 5-day blocked threshold and no time-in-state threshold, so the only possible reason is BlockedDuration on a Work Item Blocked 5+ days); that a Work Item with no time-in-state threshold never carries a TimeInState reason; and that `staleReasons[].kind` is a PascalCase string. If the read cannot reproduce what the browser's rule shows for the same Team and day (other than the instance-zone day count near midnight), the slice's hypothesis is disproved; report at the hold, do not paper over it.

End of phase 02 (slice-02 dogfood): with the same local instance, open a demo Team's Flow Overview on the current range and on a past range; the Stale count equals the number of `isStale: true` entries on the WIP read for the same day (OUT-stale-agrees). Answer DESIGN's open question by hand: after saving a changed staleness threshold in the Team settings, does the Flow Overview's WIP query refetch so the change shows at once? Record yes/no; if no, raise it at the hold rather than fixing it inside this story. Check under a throttled connection that the Stale widget, aging chart and dialogs still show WidgetShell's loading and could-not-load looks exactly as before (no new fetch is added).

Ratification at the hold before any push: ADR-240 is still 'Proposed'; the AFK maintainer decision recorded at DISTILL review, to revisit: the Flow Overview's Stale and WIP dialogs pass the range end as the Time in State column's `now`, so on a past range the 'Nd in State' label counts to the range end instead of today (02-01). Also list the existing-test rewrites and deletions each step made under paradigm_note (a).

Comments in new and touched code: rare, plain-language why, never an internal reference (no D-, DDD-, US-, AC-, UC-, UPSTREAM-, CI- or ADR- numbers). Touching a file whose comments break the rule means fixing them in the same change (PortfolioMetricsController's wip action carries several, see 01-03). The DISTILL `// SCAFFOLD: true` markers (StalenessPolicy.cs, TimeInStateBadge.tsx props) are removed by the step that makes the scaffold real.

Push order: phase 01 may be pushed on its own (each Epic ships alone; slice 01 already gives `lh --json` users the fields). Phase 02 depends on phase 01 being on main. Never push red: a step whose pending tests are not yet green keeps them skipped.
The AC-/US-/D-/DDD-/OUT- tags in this roadmap are navigation aids only; never copy them into code comments, test names or commit subjects.
Phase 02 is pushed as a whole (02-01 to 02-03), never per step: between 02-01 and 02-02 the dialog badges read the server while the Stale count still uses the browser rule.

phases.name: Lighthouse marks stale on its WIP reads
phases.description: Backend only, releasable alone. The pure policy and the walking skeleton through the Team WIP read first, then the rest of the Team read's boundaries, then the Portfolio read, then the sync-time signal onto the same policy. No frontend file is touched; every existing read is byte-for-byte unchanged except the two WIP reads gaining two optional fields.

steps.name: A flow coach reads which Work Item has sat too long in Review and why, from one pure rule
steps.description: Walking skeleton. Replace the scaffold body of StalenessPolicy.Evaluate(candidate, zone, asOfDay) with the rule: Doing only; time in state days = asOfDay - InstanceCalendar.DayOf(enteredAt, zone) + 1 (minimum 1), stale when > threshold and not Blocked; blocked days by the same arithmetic on blockedSince, stale when >= blocked threshold; 0 turns a trigger off; a Blocked item whose days in state are past the time-in-state threshold carries TimeInStateWhileBlocked without becoming stale; unknown entered day = no time-in-state reason, unknown blocked start = no blocked reason, but a Blocked item with an unknown entered day and a known blocked start is still judged by its blocked time. Then wire the Team WIP read: build StalenessPolicy.For(team) once per read and call dto.CarryStaleness(policy, clock.Zone, DateOnly.FromDateTime(asOfDate)) on each projected WorkItemDto after construction. Map StaleReason to StaleReasonDto with stateName omitted when null.
